skill.name: browser-mcp-agent
skill.description: Give an AI agent its own real browser over MCP tool calls - launch, navigate, click, fill, screenshot, extract text, run JS - with a kernel-level real-device fingerprint and a persistent profile, so the session stays logged in between runs and pages see one coherent device instead of a headless build. No Playwright or SDK code to write. Use when an agent should operate a site itself, when a computer-use / browser-use setup needs a captured real fingerprint rather than a synthetic one, when agent sessions keep losing their login, or when comparing hosted agent-browser services. Also for 'MCP browser', 'browser MCP server', 'let my agent browse the web', 'agent browser control', 'browser-use MCP', 'computer use browser', 'Browserbase alternative', 'Steel browser alternative', 'headless browser detected'. Node (npx) or Python; Windows x64, macOS Intel + Apple Silicon, Linux x64 / arm64. SDK and REST reference is anti-detect-browser; account isolation is multi-account-isolation.
skill.summary: Control a persistent, fingerprinted browser through MCP tools for authorized research, testing, and account workflows.
skill.author: antibrow

security_audit.summary: The static matches are primarily documentation examples, URLs, cache paths, and environment-variable placeholders, so they are false positives rather than executed behavior. The skill still exposes a high-impact browser with persistent sessions, page JavaScript, anti-detection features, and shareable screen access; these contextual risks require strict authorization, isolation, and human approval for consequential actions.

remediation.issue: A closed browser kernel is fetched from a vendor CDN and cached locally on first launch.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions, verify published integrity and binary provenance, prefetch during a controlled build, and review updates before deployment.

remediation.issue: Persistent profiles can retain cookies and authenticated storage across agent runs.
remediation.suggestion: Use separate throwaway profiles for untrusted sites, restrict each profile to one trust boundary, and delete sensitive profiles after use.

remediation.issue: Live View can expose an authenticated browser to anyone holding its shareable URL.
remediation.suggestion: Disable Live View by default, protect links with access controls, avoid sensitive profiles, and stop streams immediately after observation.

remediation.issue: The agent can execute JavaScript and perform browser writes.
remediation.suggestion: Expose only required MCP tools, keep navigation destinations operator-controlled, treat page content as untrusted, and require confirmation for posts, purchases, deletions, and credential changes.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent authenticated browser exposure
semantic_findings.description: The skill keeps cookies and storage in named profiles and gives an agent control over logged-in sessions. A confused or hijacked agent could perform account actions inside the retained session.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The document directly states that browser profiles persist logins and that the agent can click, fill, evaluate, and act within those sessions.

semantic_findings.title: Unprotected live screen sharing
semantic_findings.description: Live View creates a shareable URL that exposes the current browser screen, including content from the active profile. Anyone who obtains the link may view sensitive authenticated information.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly says that anyone holding the shareable link sees whatever the profile is logged into.

semantic_findings.title: Indirect prompt injection and tool-abuse exposure
semantic_findings.description: Web content is returned to the agent that chooses subsequent tool calls, creating an indirect prompt injection path. Malicious page text could redirect navigation, request secrets, or trigger browser writes despite the documented warnings.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The document identifies the agent decision loop and page-controlled text as the condition for indirect prompt injection, while the exposed tools include navigation, JavaScript evaluation, and writes.

semantic_findings.title: Closed binary supply-chain dependency
semantic_findings.description: The package fetches a closed-source browser kernel from a vendor CDN on first launch and has no offline mode. A compromised or unexpected binary update could execute with the browser process privileges.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly documents a first-launch CDN download, a closed-source kernel, local caching, and the absence of an offline mode.

content.user_title: Control A Real Browser With MCP
content.value_statement: Agents often lose login state and get blocked by headless browser signals. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a persistent fingerprinted browser they can drive through MCP tools for authorized workflows.
actual_capabilities: Launch a named browser profile with a coherent real-device fingerprint over MCP.
Navigate pages, click elements, fill forms, extract text, and capture screenshots.
Keep cookies and storage so authorized logins can continue across runs.
Optionally evaluate page JavaScript and stream a live browser view for operators.
Support Node and Python MCP configurations on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
limitations: Requires an AntiBrow API key and a first-launch download of a closed browser kernel.
Does not guarantee bypass of advanced bot detection or enforcement systems.
Alpine or musl Linux is not supported, and concurrent sessions depend on the plan limit.
Page content is untrusted input and can mislead the agent without operator controls.

use_cases.title: Authorized dashboard checks
use_cases.description: An operator asks the agent to open an owned dashboard, read key metrics, and report status without writing automation code.

use_cases.title: Bot-detection self testing
use_cases.description: A security engineer uses a real fingerprint to exercise their own site defenses and compare agent browser behavior.

use_cases.title: Guided multi-step research
use_cases.description: A researcher has the agent browse public pages, extract structured findings, and keep a throwaway profile isolated from private accounts.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner status check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use a throwaway profile, open the public status page I provide, extract the current service state, and summarize it in three bullets.
prompt_templates.scenario: First-time browser MCP use on a public page

prompt_templates.title: Authenticated account review
prompt_templates.prompt: Launch my authorized profile for our staging app, open the billing page I specify, capture the current plan and invoice status, and stop without making changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Read-only work inside an owned logged-in session

prompt_templates.title: Form fill with confirmation
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the support form on our site, fill the draft fields I provide, capture the form, and wait for my approval before submitting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Write actions that need a human checkpoint

prompt_templates.title: Advanced isolation workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create separate profiles for public research and our owned admin account. Research only in the public profile, then report findings. Never navigate the admin profile to untrusted URLs or start Live View without asking me first.
prompt_templates.scenario: Higher-risk agent browsing with trust boundaries

output_examples.input: Check the public status page and summarize service health.
output_examples.output: Opened the provided status page in a throwaway profile. API and dashboard services are operational. Incident banner is not present. No login or write actions were performed.

output_examples.input: Open our staging billing page and report the plan without changing anything.
output_examples.output: Launched the authorized staging profile and navigated only to the billing page you specified. Current plan is Pro monthly. Next invoice date is 2026-09-01. No settings were modified.

output_examples.input: Draft the support form and wait for approval before submit.
output_examples.output: Filled the subject and body fields, verified the form values on screen, and paused for confirmation. Submit action remains pending until you approve.

best_practices: Pin package versions, verify integrity, and prefetch the browser kernel in a controlled build environment.
Expose only the MCP tools required for the task and keep untrusted browsing out of logged-in profiles.
Treat page text as untrusted data and require human approval for posts, purchases, deletions, and other consequential writes.
anti_patterns: Do not leave package installation on unpinned latest or allow automatic resolution at every agent start.
Do not let the agent follow page-supplied links or start Live View on sensitive authenticated profiles.
Do not reuse one profile for both public web crawling and high-value account operations.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to drive a real fingerprinted browser through MCP tools without writing Playwright scripts.

faq.question: Do I need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The MCP server expects an AntiBrow API key from the environment, and the free plan includes one concurrent browser.

faq.question: Does the browser stay logged in?
faq.answer: Yes for named profiles. Cookies and storage persist so authorized sessions can continue across runs.

faq.question: Is this guaranteed to avoid bot detection?
faq.answer: No. A coherent real-device fingerprint reduces synthetic-browser signals, but network reputation and behavior still matter.

faq.question: Is it safe to browse untrusted websites?
faq.answer: Only with isolation. Use a throwaway profile, limit tools, and treat all page content as untrusted agent input.

faq.question: Which platforms are supported?
faq.answer: Windows x64, macOS Intel and Apple Silicon, and Linux x64 or arm64 with glibc are supported. Alpine or musl is not supported yet.
